articles.title: ‘Jimi Horsedrix brought me so much joy’: the comic drawing a horse a day – and day 69’s is unsuitable for children
articles.summary: On day 58, he did a boxing Ali horse. On day 67, he did a howling horse. So what made Andy Field suddenly decide to draw 100 equines? And what made day 48’s so phallic?
body: A ndy Field was midway through his standup run at this year’s Edinburgh fringe when he was struck by an unusual urge – the urge to draw a horse. “I hadn’t sat down to draw anything since I was at school,” says the 34-year-old comedian. “Drawing was a skill I didn’t have.”

He’s not lying. The subsequent horse Field posted to TikTok and Instagram was rather naive, with its four identical straight legs and cartoon eyeball. But the project he announced alongside it – Drawing a Horse Every Day Until I’m Really Good at Drawing Horses – immediately captured people’s hearts. Over a million people watched the minute-long video of him drawing that first horse with a four-colour ballpoint pen. By day three – an undeniably terrible effort in which the horse appeared to have sprouted a platypus’s bill – more than two million, by his estimation, had tuned in. “People were willing the series to continue,” says Field. And so he did.
points: So what made Andy Field suddenly decide to draw 100 equines?

articles.title: After Martha Stewart’s Halloween homeless costume disaster, I have to know: celebrities, why do you risk it? | Coco Khan
articles.summary: Cynics might say it’s about courting controversy, but I think these fancy dress faux-pas hint at a bleaker truth. It’s not easy being an optimist these days. It requires practice, like exercising a muscle.
body: And so it is that this week I find my optimism being put through its paces by the news of US superstar homemaker Martha Stewart and her offensive Halloween costume of a homeless person, complete with a dirt-smeared face and a sign reading “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!”.

How’s this for a more upbeat interpretation: she is preparing for her next chapter as an edgy, anti-humour one-woman act known as Martha Stewart Lee. I can see it now: her Fringe show – which I am calling Laundered – receiving rave reviews. “After decades of perfect tablescapes, Martha Stewart serves up something truly unpalatable: herself.” Five stars!

Before influencers made “being a Pinterest board made flesh” a viable career, there was Stewart. Arguably the US’s national authority on doing domestic things properly, Stewart, now 85, built an empire of cookbooks, magazines, TV shows and homeware. In 1999, she took her company public and became a billionaire. Then, in 2004, she was convicted of conspiracy, obstruction of an agency proceeding and making false statements to federal investigators, and served five months in prison.
points: Cynics might say it’s about courting controversy, but I think these fancy dress faux-pas hint at a bleaker truth.

articles.title: ‘It’s just vape shops, nail shops, charity shops’: can anything save the British high street?
articles.summary: It’s 20 years since Jo and Richard Hill bought anything in Rotherham town centre. Why have they and so many locals abandoned it for the nearest retail park – and what would it take to change their minds? On 22 May 1987, retail history was made in Rotherham.
body: Almost 40 years on, the razzle is a bit less dazzling. Parkgate, as the retail park is called now, looks like any large big-box outdoor shopping centre you might find on urban fringes. There’s a Primark, a Sports Direct and a Matalan, plus (of course) a Frankie & Benny’s. Shoppers still seem to love it. “I think it’s ideal. It’s got everything here,” says Robert Gordon. The 66-year-old retired factory production manager had popped to Pets at Home to get a cupcake and toy for his dog Bruno’s fourth birthday.

Gordon has lived in Rotherham for 24 years. “A lot of people come to outlets like this. It’s very rare we go into the town centre and, if we did, we’d go to Sheffield,” he says. He is hardly an outlier. Almost half of Britons don’t visit their high street weekly. Instead, shoppers are opting for retail parks. Business is so strong, retailers are scrambling for spots, even paying extra to secure their place. By the end of 2025, only 4.8% of retail park lots in Britain were vacant, according to real estate consultancy Knight Frank – the lowest level on record. Vacancy rates for UK high streets, on the other hand, sit at 13%, reports Savills.
points: It’s 20 years since Jo and Richard Hill bought anything in Rotherham town centre.
Why have they and so many locals abandoned it for the nearest retail park – and what would it take to change their minds?

articles.title: Mexican Seafood and Natural Wines Are in the Spotlight at This New NYC Restaurant
articles.summary: Known for their roasted and slow-cooked meats at Taqueria Ramirez, Tania Apolinar and Giovanni Cervantes partnered with chef Carlos Barrera to open a new seafood-focused wine bar this year. Here’s what a full day of prep looks like at El Camarón Peludo in the West Village.
body: First, fresh shrimp from Sinaloa, Mexico; Ecuador; and more locales are de-shelled and de-veined for three central shrimp dishes. Then, Cervantes starts the fresh salsa for the day, taste testing and comparing each batch to the salsa from last week to make sure the flavor is consistent. A bright red salsa is mixed with mayo to create the sauce on the camarones zarandeados, a shrimp version of a fish dish from the Pacific coast of Mexico that is usually grilled in a flat wire grill basket.

Upstairs, Apolinar prepares the wine bar for opening, laying out chilled seafood on ice in the window and wine bottles that will be placed in chilled buckets for service. She recommends sitting at the long, winding bar to watch the bartenders and chefs work.

articles.title: Georgia Governor-Elect Keisha Lance Bottoms Celebrated Her Historic Win in Full Fuchsia
articles.summary: The pink pantsuit was a bright, joyous choice, marking a new chapter in Georgia’s gubernatorial record—and cementing the exuberant energy of Tuesday evening.
body: Yesterday evening, amid the midterms’ historic blue sweep, former mayor of Atlanta Keisha Lance Bottoms was elected governor of Georgia—making her the first Democratic governor of Georgia in this millennium and the first Black woman elected governor in United States history.

To celebrate that momentous occasion, Bottoms donned a fuchsia pantsuit with a matching silk shirt underneath designed by Dedrick Thomas of Hideoki Bespoke in Georgia. It was a bright, joyous choice, marking a new chapter in Georgia’s gubernatorial record and reflecting the exuberant energy of the evening overall.

“This campaign was about every community and every corner of Georgia,” Bottoms said in her victory speech at the Marriott Marquis in downtown Atlanta. (She’d been introduced by her daughter, Lennox, wearing a matching pink ensemble.) “No matter who you voted for tonight, I will be a governor for all of Georgia.”

articles.title: Deb Haaland and Peggy Flanagan Mark Their Historic Wins in Intentional Earrings
articles.summary: Both politicians wore statement earrings made by Indigenous artists, a thoughtful move to uplift and spotlight the unique beauty found within their communities.
body: Haaland—who is a Laguna Pueblo congresswoman and the former interior secretary under Joe Biden’s administration—made an appearance in Albuquerque, New Mexico. She wore a pair of titanium dragonfly earrings by Pat Pruitt, a Laguna and Chiricahua Apache artist based in the state. Along with spotlighting one of the Native community’s most well-known artists, her choice to wear dragonfly earrings was also symbolic: They represented taking flight, change, and transformation.

The dragonfly earrings are one of Pruitt’s signature pieces, though he also specializes in sleek cuffs and necklaces, too. “The first version of the dragonfly earrings debuted in 2015, heavily influenced by the work of fashion designer Pilar Agoyo (Ohkay Owingeh/Cochiti/Kewa Pueblos) and my mentor, Greg Lewis (Laguna Pueblo),” says Pruitt of Haaland’s earrings. “The design brought together the traditional double-cross motif Greg taught me and the bold, black dragonfly imagery Pilar was incorporating into her work at the time. Titanium has since become my material of choice, allowing me to produce the earrings in a variety of colors.”
points: Both politicians wore statement earrings made by Indigenous artists, a thoughtful move to uplift and spotlight the unique beauty found within their communities.

According to Austin John Plays, Ocarina of Time already ships with a weird glitch that won't necessarily break your experience, but which may slow it down for a while, and perhaps even confuse players into thinking something is wrong with their game or their console.

As his post explains, if you're playing the physical copy of Ocarina of Time, and it's the first game you've ever played on your Switch 2—maybe you got one of those fancy new Zelda anniversary consoles and want to break it in properly?—you may run into glaring performance issues: The game may freeze, your controller may stop working, and the FPS may drop to single digits.

articles.title: Your Android Can Get Hacked Without You Doing Anything at All
articles.summary: You probably know that clicking suspicious links online or opening attachments from strangers in an email or text is a recipe for hacking. It's a dangerous world out there online, so it's always important to be vigilant. However, the danger doesn't always involve something you do.
body: As reported by The Hacker News, there is a critical Android security flaw that could enable remote code execution on your device. In other words, bad actors could use the flaw to run their own code on your phone, effectively taking over the device for their own gain. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-58868, isn't universal, but it is widespread: It currently affects Android 14 through Android 17, the latest version of Google's OS. If your phone runs Android 12 or Android 13, it may be unaffected, as Google doesn't identify these versions in its security bulletin, but it doesn't explicitly rule them out, either.

articles.title: A Night of Firsts: The History-Making Victories Across the 2026 Midterm Elections
articles.summary: The 2026 midterm elections delivered remarkable political milestones, from the first Black woman to be elected governor in U.S. history to the first Native American woman elected to the Senate.
body: It took 94 years for Kansas to elect another Democratic U.S. senator. It took the entire history of the United States for a Black woman to be elected governor. Both happened on Tuesday night—two significant milestones amid a night of major triumphs, firsts, and history-making moments.

And it was true that the gubernatorial races sent shockwaves from state to state. In California, Xavier Becerra, the former U.S. secretary of health and human services, became the first Latino ever elected governor of the state. And both Nevada and Wisconsin elected their first Black governors: Attorney General Aaron Ford and Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, respectively. Minnesota elected its first woman governor in Amy Klobuchar, who will leave behind her seat in the U.S. Senate after two decades. And in Ohio, former state health director Amy Acton defeated Republican Vivek Ramaswamy to become the first woman elected governor in the state’s history.
points: The 2026 midterm elections delivered remarkable political milestones, from the first Black woman to be elected governor in U.S. history to the first Native American woman elected to the Senate.
